newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola, flax end lower, wheat, barley higher.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola, flax end lower, wheat, barley higher.

text.p: WCE canola futures closed lower, pressured by lower CBOT soybean futures and forecasts for beneficial rain in Brazilian soybean areas, traders said.
Flaxseed followed canola lower, while feed wheat and feed barley ended higher on ideas the current cold spell in the Prairie provinces will boost livestock feed consumption.
Poor export demand also weighed on canola. Traders said canola is too expensive and discouraging foreign buyers.
Canola closed down $2.50 to $1.80 with March off $2.50 at $409.20 per tonne. Flaxseed closed down $0.50 to $1.80 with March off $1.00 at $351.50.

In wheat, the cold Canadian weather plus gains in U.S. wheat futures encouraged buying. Wheat closed up $0.20 to $1.20 with March up $0.20 at $170.70. Barley closed up $0.20 to $0.90 with February up $0.50 at $139.10.
Oats did not trade and only October feed peas traded up US$0.80 at US$187.00.
(All values in Canadian dollars/tonne except peas, oats)
